note: Nothing on this list has been implemented. Each item needs your choice (option A/B/C or 'defer') before work starts. 'Benefit' and 'Cost' are the author's assessment, not verified facts.

rows.suggestion: Build a multi-season injury history from the official NFL weekly injury report (weeks and seasons on the nfl.com selector).
rows.benefit: Needed for any backtest of injury-based signals.
rows.cost: Unestimated; depends on archival coverage, formats, and permitted access.
options: A: Collect 2026 weeks 1-10 first, then decide

rows.suggestion: Create a source-backed replacement-chain register for offense and defense, with separate second-, third-, and fourth-string slots. Populate a tier only when an official source establishes it; use game-book participation to check who actually played. Do not treat a roster page, injury report, or headline as proof of depth order.
rows.benefit: Makes the requested backup tiers visible without inferring assignments or impact from absences.
rows.cost: Unestimated; depends on whether official sources expose explicit depth order and participation evidence.
options: A: Locate primary depth-order sources first
B: Keep the blank tracker until verified records are available

rows.suggestion: Evaluate licensed sportsbook-odds data vendors (opening and closing lines, props) with written licence terms.
rows.benefit: Enables closing-line value (CLV) and real validation.
rows.cost: Unknown; request written coverage, licence terms, and pricing before selecting a provider.
options: A: Evaluate vendors and report cost
B: Use public data only (see SG-04)

rows.suggestion: Check any proposed public odds/outcome datasets for publisher, licence, timestamp quality, and season coverage before use. Official NFL schedule/stat pages can help catalogue outcomes but do not supply the historical market dataset required here.
rows.benefit: May identify candidate datasets; none is approved until the publisher, terms, and coverage are checked.
rows.cost: Unknown; confirm access, completeness, and reuse terms.

rows.suggestion: Freeze the validation rules (gates G0-G8 on the Strategies page) before testing, and choose the primary metric (CLV, ROI, or Brier score).
rows.benefit: Makes the evaluation protocol explicit before results are inspected; no threshold is prescribed here.
options: A: Primary metric = CLV; ROI secondary
B: Primary metric = Brier score / calibration; ROI secondary

rows.suggestion: Review the current NFL.com Terms and any location-specific additional terms before any automated collection or redistribution; systematic retrieval requires express written consent under the reviewed terms.
options: A: Check terms, then decide on automation

rows.suggestion: Decide whether GitHub Pages deployment should be gated on both site-verification jobs. Verification currently runs independently on pull requests and main pushes; do not add automated NFL data retrieval without permission.
rows.benefit: Makes publication policy explicit while retaining the existing source and link checks.
rows.cost: Low; adjust workflow dependencies only if the reviewer chooses to gate deployment.
options: A: Require both site verifiers before Pages deploy
B: Keep verification and deployment independent; monitor both

rows.suggestion: Make tables sortable and searchable by team, player, status and unit on each page.
rows.benefit: Faster review of the injury data.
rows.source: User brief (usability request; not an external factual claim)

rows.suggestion: Decide the intended use: research only, paper trading, or real-money use. If real money is considered, obtain qualified legal and compliance advice for the relevant jurisdiction before proceeding.
rows.benefit: Removes legal risk before any money moves.
rows.cost: Unknown; request scope and fees from qualified counsel for the applicable jurisdiction.
options: A: Research and paper trading only (no real money)
B: Real money after legal opinion
